item: X-U1 Regulator-sourced year-by-year count of AI-derived INDs 2018-2026
queries_tried: "AI-discovered" OR "AI-derived" molecules entering clinical trials per year cumulative 2016 2018 2020 2022 2024 annual number first-in-human | number of AI-discovered drug molecules in clinical trials by year 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 growth pipeline count doubling | "AI-first" biotech "15" molecules in clinical trials March 2022 BCG Wellcome 150 discovery pipeline Jayatunga coming wave | FDA IND tagged by discovery method AI provenance field
failure_reason: No regulator records discovery method on an IND, and no clinical registry carries an AI-provenance field, so no official annual series exists. Every available count is a private census with a self-set inclusion rule, and the four accessible anchors use three different rules (AI-native company assets; AI-enabled including pharma partnerships; AI-discovered with documented clinical outcomes).
alt_sources_tried: BCG/Nature Reviews Drug Discovery landing page (HTTP 403); Science AAAS blog 'AI Drugs So Far' (HTTP 403); OECD AI in Science chapter (HTTP 403); Frontiers in Pharmacology 2026 review (fetched, gives programme-level not annual counts); ScienceDirect Niazi 2024 census (abstract only)
best_estimate: Cumulative AI-derived clinical-stage molecules: about 15 in early 2022, 67 in April 2024, over 75 at end-2024, 117 in December 2025; implied doubling time 1.2-2.1 years, central 1.5 years
best_estimate_basis: Four independent census anchors [E-9516 and Agent B E-2054/E-2071/E-2072 lineage], pairwise doubling times computed in [E-9517]. The definitional drift between anchors biases the ratio upward, so the doubling time is a lower bound on the true doubling interval; every plausible tightening of the inclusion rule lowers both endpoints and leaves the interval roughly intact.

item: X-U2 Measured effect of AI on clinical development design decisions (dose, endpoint, population)
queries_tried: FDA Project Optimus dose optimization oncology inadequate dose selection cause of phase 3 failure percentage post-marketing dose changes | in silico clinical trials virtual control arm regulatory qualification model-informed drug development replacing patients 2026 FDA | AI trial design endpoint selection measured effect success rate controlled comparison
failure_reason: The literature measures AI applied to patient matching and to protocol operational burden. No study located measures whether AI-assisted dose, endpoint or population selection changes the probability that a pivotal trial succeeds, which is the channel with the largest plausible effect and no measurement.
alt_sources_tried: ASCO/JCO Project Optimus postmarketing-requirement analysis (abstract only, no AI arm); EMA virtual control group draft qualification opinion (preclinical scope only); FDA/EMA ten Guiding Principles of Good AI Practice January 2026 (principles, no effect size); Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics 2025 review of AI-driven clinical trials (descriptive)
best_estimate: No controlled measurement exists as of August 2026; the size of the addressable problem is bounded by the 48 percent of Phase III patients requiring dose modification at the Phase I recommended dose
best_estimate_basis: [E-9531] bounds the size of the design-error class. Absent any measured AI effect, the honest position is that this channel is unmeasured rather than absent, and that the Amdahl ceiling derived from discovery's share of time and cost does not bound it, because a clinical-design improvement acts inside the clinical stages.

item: X-U3 Published elasticity of a health-outcome measure, rather than approval count, to any pipeline factor
queries_tried: elasticity of annual drug approvals to R&D input published estimate | health outcome per approved drug quality-adjusted life years produced per approval trend | Deloitte forecast asset value per approval outcome-weighted productivity measure
failure_reason: The entire elasticity framework in this run, and in the published literature it draws on, uses annual approvals as system output. No published study estimates the elasticity of an outcome-weighted measure (life-years, QALYs, or burden-of-disease displaced) to any pipeline factor, so the distortion introduced by counting approvals cannot be quantified.
alt_sources_tried: Deloitte annual R&D returns series (asset-value based, not outcome based); Norstella/Citeline productivity analyses (approval-count based); the Japanese conditional-approval withdrawal record, which demonstrates the distortion exists but does not size it
best_estimate: The distortion is material and directionally tilts any approval-count ranking toward factors that raise the count of small single-arm rare-disease approvals and away from factors that raise effect size in common disease
best_estimate_basis: Reasoning from the Japanese case in Agent E's regional section, where two of five conditional approvals were withdrawn after confirmatory failure, so that route raised the approval count and lowered durable output. No number is asserted.

item: X-U4 Count of programmes started that would not have started absent AI structure prediction
queries_tried: AI enabled previously undruggable targets new programs started structure prediction opened targets that could not be prosecuted evidence 2025 2026 | AlphaFold impact measured drug discovery new targets structures enabled 2024 2025 critique limited impact hit rate | number of novel first-in-class drug targets entering clinical development per year trend 2010 2020 unique targets in clinical pipeline growth
failure_reason: The counterfactual is not recorded by anyone. Reviews assert that AI is expanding the druggable space but none counts programmes attributable to a predicted structure, and the aggregate trend runs the other way, with novel targets entering the pipeline falling to 30 in 2024.
alt_sources_tried: Nature Biotechnology 'Redefining druggable targets with artificial intelligence' (assertive, no counterfactual count); Chemical Reviews 'Computer-Aided Drug Discovery for Undruggable Targets' (methodological); DeepMind five-years-of-impact post (usage statistics, not programme counts); L.E.K. novel-target series (counts novel targets but does not attribute them to AI)
best_estimate: Zero to low tens of programmes as of 2026, and not distinguishable from zero in the aggregate novel-target series
best_estimate_basis: The aggregate series moves the wrong way for a large effect: novel targets entering the pipeline fell from about 100 a year to 30 in 2024 while the pipeline doubled [E-9509]. If AI-enabled structures were opening targets at scale, that series would not be falling. This is the single measurement that would most sharpen finding X-01, in either direction.

item: X-U5 Exact current entry count of FDA's Table of Surrogate Endpoints
queries_tried: FDA table of surrogate endpoints used as basis of approval number of entries 2024 2025 adult surrogate endpoint table count | fda.gov table-surrogate-endpoints-were-basis-drug-approval-or-licensure
failure_reason: The FDA page states the table exists and is updated roughly twice a year; secondary sources give 'over 200' without a dated count, and fda.gov returns HTTP 401/403 to the available fetch tooling in this environment, as Agents A, E and F independently recorded.
alt_sources_tried: FDA table page (401/403 to fetch tool); Federation of American Scientists analysis (gives 'over 200', no dated count); Kelley Drye analysis of the accelerated approval draft guidance (qualitative); Journal of Law, Medicine and Ethics review (qualitative)
best_estimate: Over 200 entries across adult and paediatric sections as of 2025
best_estimate_basis: [E-9528], corroborated by Agent E's independent recovery of the same figure from a different route. The precision does not matter for finding X-14: the argument turns on the accepted set being one to two orders of magnitude larger than the 11 formally qualified biomarkers, which holds at any count above about 100.

item: X-U6 Like-for-like comparison of registrational trial capacity, China versus United States
queries_tried: China share of global first-in-human oncology trial starts 2024 2025 percent versus United States trial initiations | China clinical trial registrations growth 2015 2025 number of new drug clinical trials initiated China per year CDE registry | FDA acceptance China-only clinical trial data sintilimab ODAC 2022 multiregional clinical trial requirement applicability US population
failure_reason: Published comparisons count all trials or all oncology trials. None separates registrational trials intended to support a US or EU marketing application from domestically-intended trials, which is the quantity that determines whether the pivotal ceiling relocates.
alt_sources_tried: CDE 2024 annual clinical trial report via Covington (gives 337 multiregional of 2,539 innovative-drug trials, which is the closest available proxy); ITIF June 2026 report (shares, not registrational counts); ESMO Open globalisation-of-oncology-trials analysis (geographic distribution, not registrational intent); Clinical Trials Arena analyst commentary (shares only)
best_estimate: Chinese registrational capacity aimed at US or EU filings is roughly 13 percent of Chinese innovative-drug trials, so the pivotal ceiling relocates far less than the total-trial ceiling does
best_estimate_basis: 337 multiregional of 2,539 innovative-drug trials in 2024 = 13.3 percent [E-9519], combined with the ODAC 14-1 vote requiring a US-applicable trial for a China-only pivotal dataset [E-9523]. This is the load-bearing quantity behind the partial verdict on finding X-13 and it is a proxy rather than a direct measurement.
